newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold seen drifting higher in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Gold seen drifting higher in slow trade.

text.p: Gold was higher in early Wednesday trading in Europe, with dealers expecting prices to drift higher in lacklustre business before today's FOMC meeting.
Gold was quoted at $382.60/$382.90 an ounce, up from $381.50/$382.00 at the London close.
One trader said gold's inability to break decisively through $383 yesterday was not a good sign for bulls, but added the metal was likely to fluctuate in a $382/$384 band.
"Customer business is rather restrained, but there is no sign of producers in the market," this trader said.
"I think we will move up slightly," another dealer said, seeing the upper end of gold's range at $383.50.
Silver edged up to $4.89/$4.91 from $4.86/$4.88, and some traders saw it advancing toward the $5.00 mark in the medium term.
Platinum eased to $387.50/$388.50 from $387.75/$388.75, while palladium was steady at $117.75/$118.75.
